territorial_scope.description: Applies to persons exercising the influence activity in France, and reaches non-EU persons whose activity targets a public established in France.

evidence.quote: visant notamment un public établi sur le territoire français

summary.short: Adopted 9 June 2023: regulates paid commercial influence by electronic means. Requires disclosure labels, bans promotion of certain products (cosmetic procedures, nicotine, certain financial products, sports betting advice), sets influencer-agent, contract, joint liability and insurance duties, and platform notice duties.
summary.long: Defines commercial influence by electronic means as paid promotion of goods, services or causes to an online audience (Art. 1) and regulates it. Art. 3 applies advertising rules to influencers. Art. 4 bans promotion of cosmetic procedures, therapeutic substitutes, nicotine products, animal promotion outside listed species, certain financial products and sports betting advice, and allows gambling promotion only where under-18s can be excluded; breaches carry two years' imprisonment and a 300,000 euro fine. Art. 5 requires 'Publicité' or 'Collaboration commerciale' labels and labels for retouched and AI-generated images. Art. 6 makes sellers liable to buyers. Arts. 7-9 regulate influencer agents, require written contracts on pain of nullity, impose joint liability on advertisers and influencers, and require non-EU persons to appoint an EU legal representative and hold insurance. Title II: Arts. 10-12 add platform notice, trusted-flagger and removal-order duties under the EU Digital Services Act; Art. 13 sets Consumer Code injunction penalty limits; Art. 14 extends financial-promotion sanctions to online promoters; Art. 15 requires platform commitments; Art. 16 adds education on commercial manipulation; Art. 17 orders a report within two years. Art. 18 bars Arts. 10-12 and 15 from taking effect before EU notification clearance.
